framework.name: Swiss nDSG
framework.description: Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection (nDSG / revDSG) — in force 1 September 2023. Aligns with GDPR principles with Swiss-specific obligations for controllers and processors.

objects.title: General Principles
objects.description: Lawfulness, purpose limitation, data minimisation, accuracy, and storage limitation principles.

objects.title: Data Subject Rights
objects.description: Rights of data subjects including access, rectification, erasure, portability, and automated decision protections.

objects.title: Controller Obligations
objects.description: Privacy by design, processing agreements, records of processing activities, DPIAs, and DPA appointment.

objects.title: Cross-Border Transfers
objects.description: Requirements for transferring personal data to third countries and permitted derogations.

objects.title: Security & Breach
objects.description: Technical and organisational security measures and data breach notification obligations.

objects.title: Enforcement & DPO
objects.description: Cooperation with the FDPIC, accountability documentation, and sanctions awareness.

objects.title: Lawfulness of Processing
objects.description: Personal data is processed lawfully (consent, contract, legal obligation, legitimate interest), proportionately, and for a defined purpose.

objects.title: Purpose Limitation
objects.description: Personal data is collected for a specified, explicit, and legitimate purpose and not processed in a manner incompatible with that purpose.

objects.title: Data Minimisation
objects.description: Only personal data that is necessary for the purpose of processing is processed.

objects.title: Accuracy
objects.description: Personal data is accurate and, where necessary, kept up to date.

objects.title: Storage Limitation
objects.description: Personal data is kept in a form which permits identification of data subjects for no longer than necessary.

objects.title: Right to Information
objects.description: Data subjects are informed about the collection of their personal data in a concise, transparent, and easily accessible form.

objects.title: Right of Access
objects.description: Data subjects have the right to obtain confirmation of whether personal data concerning them is being processed and to receive a copy.

objects.title: Right to Rectification
objects.description: Data subjects have the right to obtain rectification of inaccurate personal data without undue delay.

objects.title: Right to Erasure
objects.description: Data subjects have the right to obtain erasure of personal data where processing is no longer necessary or lawful.

objects.title: Right to Data Portability
objects.description: Data subjects have the right to receive personal data in a structured, commonly used, and machine-readable format.

objects.title: Automated Decisions
objects.description: Data subjects are not subject to decisions based solely on automated processing without appropriate safeguards and the ability to request human review.

objects.title: Privacy by Design and Default
objects.description: Technical and organisational measures ensure data protection principles are implemented by design and by default.

objects.title: Data Processing Agreements
objects.description: Contracts with processors include mandatory provisions for data protection, instructions, confidentiality, security, and audit rights.

objects.title: Records of Processing Activities
objects.description: A record of processing activities is maintained covering purposes, categories of data, recipients, and retention periods.

objects.title: Data Protection Impact Assessment
objects.description: A DPIA is carried out for high-risk processing operations before processing commences.

objects.title: Data Protection Advisor
objects.description: A data protection advisor (DPA) is appointed where required; their contact details are published.

objects.title: Adequacy of Third Country
objects.description: Personal data is transferred to third countries only where an adequate level of protection is guaranteed (adequacy decision or appropriate safeguards).

objects.title: Standard Contractual Clauses
objects.description: Where no adequacy decision exists, standard contractual clauses or binding corporate rules approved by the FDPIC are used.

objects.title: Derogations
objects.description: Transfers not covered by adequacy decisions are based on explicit consent, contract performance, or vital interests where permitted.

objects.title: Technical and Organisational Measures
objects.description: Appropriate technical and organisational security measures are implemented to protect personal data against accidental or unlawful processing, loss, or destruction.

objects.title: Breach Notification to FDPIC
objects.description: Data breaches likely to result in high risk to data subjects are reported to the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC) without delay.

objects.title: Breach Notification to Data Subjects
objects.description: Data subjects are notified of high-risk breaches without undue delay if notification is necessary to protect their interests.

objects.title: FDPIC Cooperation
objects.description: Full cooperation is provided to the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner during investigations and audits.

objects.title: Accountability and Documentation
objects.description: The controller can demonstrate compliance with nDSG through appropriate documentation, policies, and audit evidence.

objects.title: Sanctions Awareness
objects.description: Personnel with data processing responsibilities are aware of potential criminal sanctions under Art. 60–66 nDSG for intentional violations.
